newsitem.title: JAPAN: One-two on prices to clobber Japan's top oil firms.
newsitem.headline: One-two on prices to clobber Japan's top oil firms.

text.p: Japanese oil firms expect their profits this year to be hit hard by a "one-two" combination of high crude oil prices and poor domestic oil product prices, a government survey showed on Monday.

Current profits of 12 leading oil firms fell 54.1 percent to a total 28 billion yen ($252 million) in the April-September half year, compared with the previous half year, said a survey by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
For the whole of fiscal 1996/97, ending next March, current profits at the 12 firms are expected to fall 32.5 percent to a combined 85 billion yen ($765 million), the ministry said.

The dozen firms covered in the survey were Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, Esso Sekiyu KK, Mobil Sekiyu KK, Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, Cosmo Oil Co Ltd, Japan Energy Corp, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, Kyushu Oil Co Ltd, Taiyo Oil Co Ltd, Nippon Oil Co Ltd Kygnus-Sekiyu KK and General Sekiyu KK.
The business term for the first three, which are affiliated with major foreign oil companies, is the calendar year.
Showa Shell is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Esso Sekiyu is a subsidiary of Exxon Corp and Mobil Sekiyu is owned by Mobil Corp.

Mobil Sekiyu and Esso Sekiyu do not announce mid-term profits. In August, Showa Shell announced a half-year profit of 5.65 billion yen ($50.9 million), against 6.35 billion yen ($57.2 million) in the previous half year.
The other nine, whose business year is April-March, will give mid-term data in late October or early November. Current profit is pre-tax, including losses or gains on investments.
The 12 cited persistent strength in global crude prices as the main reason for the profit decline, a MITI official said.
"Oil firms are suffering because they can't immediately pass on in the wholesale price higher costs from strong crude prices and the weaker yen against the dollar," he said.
The price of United Arab Emirates Dubai crude, the benchmark in Asia, has risen about $4 a barrel since early April, while the yen has weakened about four yen against the dollar during that period.
Since April, many Japanese oil firms have been basing their monthly wholesale product prices on global crude and oil product prices as well as on foreign exchange rates.

But there is a two-month delay in passing the higher costs on to the wholesale price. To set the September wholesale price, oil firms take into account crude prices and currency rates in July. "What's more, domestic oil product prices are weak," the MITI official said.
The retail price of gasoline, formerly a pillar of refiners' income, has plummetted in Japan in the past two years amid heated competition among gasoline stations.
Retailers raced to slash prices in the run-up to the deregulation of oil product imports last April, anticipating an influx of cheap imports.
Before the reforms, imports of oil products such as gasoline, kerosene and gas oil were restricted to oil refiners.

Contrary to expectations, only a few trading houses and a farmers' association have imported oil products, as rising overseas oil product prices and the weaker yen are shaving the profitability of imports.
Domestic kerosene and gas oil retail prices are gradually rising, but have not reached levels refiners are aiming for. ($1=111)
